name: Alpha#1
plain_english: For each of the last 5 days, take the close if the stock rose or the 20-day volatility if it fell, square it, and find the day with the largest value. A squared price always beats a squared volatility, so this really finds the week's highest up-day close. Score = which day that was, ranked and centered on 0. Read as "days since the peak", a fresh peak scores low (short); code that counts the other way turns it into momentum.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#2
plain_english: Over 6 days, compares two daily rankings: how much volume grew versus 2 days earlier, and how much the stock gained from open to close. Volume jumps landing on up days (hype) → short; landing on down days (panic selling) → buy.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#3
plain_english: Over 10 days, checks whether the opening price and the volume, each ranked against all stocks every day, rise and fall together. Together (a crowd piling in) → short; opposite → buy.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#4
plain_english: Ranks today's low against all stocks, then asks where that rank sits within the stock's own last 9 days. Top of its 9-day range (strong versus the market lately) → short; bottom → buy. A plain rubber-band reversal.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#5
plain_english: Multiplies two ranks: how far today's open is above the 10-day average vwap, and how far today's close is above today's vwap (made negative). All scores are 0 or below; the most negative are stocks that opened high and closed strong, which it shorts. Stocks that opened low or faded intraday sit near 0, on the buy side.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#6
plain_english: The 10-day correlation between raw opening price and raw volume, flipped. Rising together → short; moving apart → buy. The raw version of #3, so one huge-volume day can dominate it.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#7
plain_english: Acts only when today's volume is above its 20-day average. Then it bets against the 7-day price change, harder when the move is unusually large versus the stock's own last 60 days: big drop → buy, big rise → short. Every quiet stock gets -1, the lowest score.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#8
plain_english: Multiplies the sum of the last 5 opens by the sum of the last 5 returns (roughly price level × recent performance) and compares it with the same number 10 days ago. Grown → short; shrunk → buy. A reversal of the last week versus two weeks earlier.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#9
plain_english: Looks at the last 5 daily price changes. If all 5 were up, or all 5 were down, it follows today's change. On every other day, which is most days, it bets against today's change. A one-day reversal that switches off during clean streaks.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Output is in price units: divide by close (or use % changes) before comparing coins with very different prices.

name: Alpha#10
plain_english: Same as #9 with a 4-day lookback, then ranked across stocks: follow today's move during a clean 4-day streak, otherwise bet against it.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#11
plain_english: Over the last 3 days, takes the largest and the smallest gap of vwap above the close, ranks both and adds them, then multiplies by the rank of the 3-day volume change. High score = the stock kept closing below its average price while volume grew → buy.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#12
plain_english: If volume rose today, bet against today's price change; if volume fell, follow it. Volume decides whether today's move is trusted. The simplest volume-confirmed reversal in the set.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Output is in price units: divide by close (or use % changes) before comparing coins with very different prices.

name: Alpha#13
plain_english: The 5-day covariance between the close's rank and volume's rank (both versus all stocks), ranked and flipped. Like #3, but covariance keeps the size of the co-movement, not only its direction.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#14
plain_english: Takes the 3-day change in daily returns (is performance improving?), ranks it and flips it, then multiplies by the 10-day correlation of open and volume. When price and volume move together, improving stocks get shorted; when they move apart, the sign flips.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#15
plain_english: Each day, takes the 3-day correlation between the high's rank and volume's rank, ranks it, adds the last 3 days, and flips. Highs and heavy volume repeatedly arriving together → short.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#16
plain_english: Same as #13 with the day's high instead of the close: 5-day covariance of high rank and volume rank, ranked and flipped.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#17
plain_english: Multiplies three ranks: how close the close is to its 10-day high (made negative), how much the daily price change is speeding up, and how unusual volume is versus normal over 5 days. Most negative (short) when a stock is at a 10-day high, accelerating, on heavy volume.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#18
plain_english: Adds three things and flips: how bumpy the daily candle bodies (close minus open) were over 5 days, today's candle body, and how closely close and open tracked each other over 10 days. Big up candles, jumpy bodies and tight open-close tracking → short.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#19
plain_english: Bets against the direction of the last 7 days' price change, sized by 1 plus the rank of the 1-year return. Short-term reversal, bet harder on long-term winners.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#20
formula: (((-1 * rank((open - delay(high, 1)))) * rank((open - delay(close, 1)))) * rank((open - delay(low, 1))))
plain_english: Compares today's open with yesterday's high, close and low, ranks each gap, and multiplies them with a minus sign. Opening above all three (a strong gap up) gives the most negative score → short; a gap down sits near 0, on the buy side.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Uses open vs yesterday's close. Crypto trades 24/7, so today's open is almost exactly yesterday's close and this gap is ~0 noise.

name: Alpha#21
plain_english: A mini Bollinger band. If the 2-day average close is above the 8-day average plus one 8-day standard deviation → -1 (short); below the 8-day average minus one standard deviation → +1 (buy). Inside the band: +1 if volume is at or above its 20-day average, else -1. Output is only +1 or -1.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#22
plain_english: How much the 5-day correlation between the high and volume has risen over the last 5 days, times the rank of 20-day price volatility, flipped. A strengthening high-volume link → short, especially in volatile stocks.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#23
plain_english: Only when today's high is above its 20-day average high: bet against the 2-day change in the high. Every other stock gets 0. Fades fresh pushes above the recent range.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Output is in price units: divide by close (or use % changes) before comparing coins with very different prices.

name: Alpha#24
plain_english: Checks the long trend: how much the 100-day average price rose over 100 days, as a share of the price 100 days ago. 5% or less (weak trend) → short in proportion to how far the price is above its 100-day low. Stronger uptrend → bet against the last 3 days' change.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Output is in price units: divide by close (or use % changes) before comparing coins with very different prices.

name: Alpha#25
plain_english: Multiplies minus today's return, 20-day dollar volume, vwap, and the distance from the close down from the high, then ranks. Stocks that fell, closed well below their high, and are large and liquid score high → buy. Because dollar volume and price are multiplied in, big expensive stocks dominate.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#26
plain_english: Each day, the 5-day correlation between where volume sits in its own 5-day range and where the high sits in its own 5-day range; takes the largest of the last 3 days and flips. Volume and highs climbing together → short.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#27
plain_english: Averages the last 2 days of the 6-day correlation between volume rank and vwap rank, then ranks across stocks. Top half → -1 (short), bottom half → +1 (buy). A two-bucket signal with nothing in between.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#28
plain_english: Adds the 5-day correlation of 20-day dollar volume with the low to the gap between the day's midpoint, (high + low) / 2, and the close, then scales. Closing below the midpoint → high score, buy; closing near the high → short.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#29
plain_english: Many layers (ranks, a log, a scale, a 2-day min, a 5-day min) wrapped around one core: minus the 5-day price change. Plus a small term: where the return from 6 days ago, flipped, sits in its 5-day range. In effect a smoothed 5-day reversal; most layers barely change the ordering.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#30
formula: (((1.0 - rank(((sign((close - delay(close, 1))) + sign((delay(close, 1) - delay(close, 2)))) + sign((delay(close, 2) - delay(close, 3)))))) * sum(volume, 5)) / sum(volume, 20))
plain_english: Adds the signs of the last 3 daily price changes (up = +1, down = -1), ranks the total, and takes 1 minus that rank, so three up days score low. Multiplies by the share of the last 20 days' volume traded in the last 5. Buys recent losers, more so when volume is concentrated in the last week.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#31
plain_english: Adds three parts: a smoothed, many-times-ranked reversal of the 10-day price change, a ranked reversal of the 3-day change, and +1 or -1 depending on whether dollar volume and the low moved together over 12 days. Mainly buys stocks that fell over 3 and 10 days.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#32
plain_english: Two scaled parts: the 7-day average close minus today's close (below the average → buy), plus 20 times the 230-day correlation between vwap and the close 5 days earlier. The first is mean reversion to a moving average; the second, weighted heavily, favors stocks whose prices move smoothly over the long run.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#33
plain_english: Ranks open divided by close, minus 1. Fell during the day (close below open) → high rank, buy; rose intraday → short. A pure one-day intraday reversal (the power of 1 does nothing).
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#34
plain_english: Adds two parts and ranks: 1 minus the rank of 2-day volatility over 5-day volatility (calming down → higher), and 1 minus the rank of today's price change (fell → higher). Buys stocks that fell today while their volatility settles.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#35
plain_english: Multiplies three time-series ranks: volume versus its own last 32 days (high is good), 1 minus close + high - low versus its last 16 days (low is good), and 1 minus today's return versus its last 32 days (low is good). Buys stocks that are weak by their own standards on unusually heavy volume.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#36
formula: (((((2.21 * rank(correlation((close - open), delay(volume, 1), 15))) + (0.7 * rank((open - close)))) + (0.73 * rank(Ts_Rank(delay((-1 * returns), 6), 5)))) + rank(abs(correlation(vwap, adv20, 6)))) + (0.6 * rank((((sum(close, 200) / 200) - open) * (close - open)))))
plain_english: A blend of five ranks with hand-set weights: 15-day correlation of the candle body with yesterday's volume (2.21), today's drop from open to close (0.7), a reversed return from 6 days ago (0.73), the absolute 6-day correlation of vwap and dollar volume (1), and the 200-day average minus the open, times the candle body (0.6). Mostly price-volume with reversal add-ons.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#37
plain_english: Adds two ranks: the 200-day correlation between yesterday's intraday drop (open minus close) and today's close, and today's intraday drop. Fell during the day → higher score, buy.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#38
plain_english: Minus the rank of where the close sits in its 10-day range, times the rank of close over open. Near a 10-day high and up a lot intraday → most negative, short.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#39
plain_english: Bets against the 7-day price change, amplified when volume over the last 9 days (recent days weighted more) was light versus normal, then sized by 1 plus the rank of the 1-year return. Fades weekly moves made on thin volume, harder for long-term winners.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#40
plain_english: Minus the rank of the high's 10-day volatility, times the 10-day correlation of high and volume. Volatile stocks whose highs and volume move together → short; moving apart flips it to buy.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#41
plain_english: The geometric middle of the day's range (square root of high × low) minus vwap. Positive when most shares traded below the middle of the range → buy. One of the simplest in the set.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Output is in price units: divide by close (or use % changes) before comparing coins with very different prices.

name: Alpha#42
plain_english: Rank of vwap minus close, divided by rank of vwap plus close. Closing below the day's average price → high score, buy; closing above → short. The paper calls it a same-day (delay-0) mean-reversion alpha: it trades at the close of the day it is computed.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#43
plain_english: Multiplies two time-series ranks: today's volume over its 20-day average, versus the last 20 days; and the 7-day price drop, versus the last 8 days. Buys stocks falling hard on unusually heavy volume.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#44
plain_english: The 5-day correlation between the raw high and volume's rank (versus all stocks), flipped. Highs and relative volume rising together → short.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#45
plain_english: Multiplies three parts and flips: the rank of the 20-day average of week-old closes, the 2-day correlation of close and volume, and the rank of the 2-day correlation between 5-day and 20-day sums of closes. Driven mostly by the very short 2-day price-volume correlation.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#46
plain_english: Compares the price's speed over the last 10 days with its speed over the 10 days before, in dollars per day. Speeding up by more than $0.25 a day → -1 (short); slowing down → +1 (buy); in between → bet against today's change. The threshold is in dollars, so a $10 and a $500 stock are treated very differently.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Output is in price units: divide by close (or use % changes) before comparing coins with very different prices.

name: Alpha#47
formula: ((((rank((1 / close)) * volume) / adv20) * ((high * rank((high - close))) / (sum(high, 5) / 5))) - rank((vwap - delay(vwap, 5))))
plain_english: Relative volume (today over its 20-day average) weighted toward cheap stocks, times today's high versus its 5-day average (scaled by how far the close fell from the high), minus the rank of the 5-day change in vwap. High score for cheap stocks on heavy volume that closed off the high while their average price fell over the week → buy.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#48
formula: (indneutralize(((correlation(delta(close, 1), delta(delay(close, 1), 1), 250) * delta(close, 1)) / close), IndClass.subindustry) / sum(((delta(close, 1) / delay(close, 1))^2), 250))
plain_english: Measures over 250 days whether today's price change tends to repeat yesterday's (a correlation), multiplies it by today's change over price, subtracts the subindustry average, and divides by the 1-year sum of squared returns. Where moves tend to persist it follows today's move; where they tend to reverse it bets against it.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Needs a sector map (indneutralize): use CoinGecko categories, or skip and demean across all coins.

name: Alpha#49
plain_english: The same speed comparison as #46 with one rule: slowed down by more than $0.10 a day versus the prior 10 days → +1 (buy); otherwise bet against today's price change.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Output is in price units: divide by close (or use % changes) before comparing coins with very different prices.

name: Alpha#50
plain_english: Each day, ranks the 5-day correlation between volume rank and vwap rank; takes the highest of the last 5 days and flips. A recent strong link between volume and price → short.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#51
plain_english: The same speed comparison as #46 and #49: slowed down by more than $0.05 a day versus the prior 10 days → +1 (buy); otherwise bet against today's price change.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Output is in price units: divide by close (or use % changes) before comparing coins with very different prices.

name: Alpha#52
plain_english: Multiplies three parts: how much the 5-day low has dropped versus 5 days ago (a recent dip), the rank of the return from about 11 months ago to 1 month ago (classic long-term momentum that skips the last month), and where today's volume sits in its last 5 days. Buys dips in long-term winners on rising volume; shorts them when their lows are rising.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#53
plain_english: Measures where the close sits in the day's range as ((close - low) - (high - close)) / (close - low), and bets against its change over 9 days. Closes creeping up toward the highs versus 9 days ago → short. Blows up when the close equals the low.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#54
plain_english: Minus the close's position in the day's range (0 = at the low, 1 = at the high), times (open / close) to the 5th power. Mostly: close near the high → short, near the low → buy; the open-to-close term makes the signal stronger or weaker.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#55
plain_english: Finds where the close sits within its 12-day low-to-high range, ranks it, and takes its 6-day correlation with volume's rank, flipped. Pushing to the top of the range on rising relative volume → short.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#56
plain_english: Minus the rank of the 10-day return divided by a short recent-return total (roughly the last 4 days), times the rank of today's return × market cap. Large companies that rose today get shorted hardest. The only alpha that uses market cap; the ratio blows up when the recent total is near zero.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Needs market cap: get it from CoinGecko.

name: Alpha#57
plain_english: Close minus vwap, divided by a 2-day smoothed rank of how many days ago the 30-day closing high was, flipped. Closing above vwap → short, below → buy; the divisor scales the bet by the timing of the recent high.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#58
plain_english: Subtracts the sector average from vwap, takes its 3-day correlation with volume, smooths it over 7 days (recent days weighted more), and asks where today's value sits in its last 5 days, flipped. Sector-relative price and volume rising together → short.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Needs a sector map (indneutralize): use CoinGecko categories, or skip and demean across all coins.

name: Alpha#59
plain_english: The same recipe as #58 at the industry level with longer windows (4-day correlation, 16-day smoothing, 8-day time rank). It mixes vwap with itself (0.73 × vwap + 0.27 × vwap), which is just vwap.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Needs a sector map (indneutralize): use CoinGecko categories, or skip and demean across all coins.

name: Alpha#60
formula: (0 - (1 * ((2 * scale(rank(((((close - low) - (high - close)) / (high - low)) * volume)))) - scale(rank(ts_argmax(close, 10))))))
plain_english: Two scaled parts: where the close sits in the day's range times volume, ranked (weight 2), minus the rank of how many days ago the 10-day closing high was. Flipped, so closing near the high on heavy volume → short. Close to the classic accumulation/distribution idea.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#61
plain_english: Outputs 1 or 0. Compares the rank of how far vwap is above its 16-day low with the rank of the 17-day correlation between vwap and 180-day dollar volume. Score 1 (buy side) when the first is lower: the stock sits near its recent low relative to how tightly its price tracks liquidity.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#62
plain_english: Outputs -1 or 0. Compares the 9-day correlation of vwap with 22-day summed dollar volume against a yes/no flag for "the high and midpoint rank above the open today" (the stock traded up from its open). -1 (short) when the correlation ranks lower than that flag.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#63
plain_english: Two smoothed ranks subtracted and flipped: the 2-day change in the industry-relative close (smoothed 8 days), minus the 13-day correlation of a vwap/open blend with 37-day summed 180-day dollar volume (smoothed 12 days). Shorts stocks that rose versus their industry; buys those whose price tracks liquidity closely.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Needs a sector map (indneutralize): use CoinGecko categories, or skip and demean across all coins. adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#64
plain_english: Outputs -1 or 0. -1 (short) when the 3-day price change (mostly vwap) outranks the 16-day correlation of 12-day summed prices (mostly the low) with 12-day summed 120-day dollar volume. In effect: short recent risers whose price does not track liquidity.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#65
plain_english: Outputs -1 or 0. -1 (short) when how far the open is above its 13-day low outranks the 6-day correlation of (almost pure) vwap with 8-day summed 60-day dollar volume. Shorts stocks that have bounced far off their recent low. The 0.008 weight on the open makes the blend nearly pure vwap.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#66
plain_english: Adds two parts and flips: the rank of the smoothed 3-day change in vwap, and where a smoothed bar-shape ratio, (low - vwap) / (open - midpoint), sits in its last 6 days. Mainly shorts stocks whose average price rose over the last few days. The low is mixed with itself (0.97 × low + 0.03 × low).
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#67
plain_english: Rank of how far today's high is above the lowest high of the last 2 days, raised to the power of the rank of the 6-day correlation between sector-relative vwap and subindustry-relative dollar volume, flipped. A bigger new high → more negative (short); the power term sets how much that counts.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Needs a sector map (indneutralize): use CoinGecko categories, or skip and demean across all coins. adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#68
plain_english: Outputs -1 or 0. -1 (short) when the 1-day rise in a close/low blend outranks where the 8-day correlation of high rank and 15-day dollar volume rank sits in its last 13 days. Shorts today's risers when the price-liquidity link is weak.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#69
plain_english: Rank of the largest 2-day rise in industry-relative vwap over the last 4 days, raised to the power of where the 4-day correlation of a close/vwap blend with dollar volume sits in its last 9 days, flipped. Recent jumps versus the industry → short.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Needs a sector map (indneutralize): use CoinGecko categories, or skip and demean across all coins. adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#70
plain_english: Rank of the 1-day change in vwap, raised to the power of where the 17-day correlation of industry-relative close with 50-day dollar volume sits in its last 17 days, flipped. Today's risers → short; the power term tunes the strength.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Needs a sector map (indneutralize): use CoinGecko categories, or skip and demean across all coins. adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#71
plain_english: The larger of two time-series ranks: the smoothed 18-day correlation between the close's 3-day position and 180-day dollar volume's 12-day position (ranked over 15 days), and a smoothed, squared rank of (low + open) minus twice vwap (ranked over 4 days). High when either the price-liquidity link is unusually strong or the low and open sit well above vwap → buy.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#72
plain_english: A ratio of two smoothed ranks: the 8-day correlation of the day's midpoint with 40-day dollar volume, divided by the 6-day correlation between vwap's 3-day position and volume's 18-day position. High when the slow price-liquidity link is strong but the fast price-volume link is weak → buy.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#73
plain_english: The larger of two signals, flipped: the rank of the smoothed 4-day change in vwap, and where the smoothed 2-day percentage drop of an open/low blend sits in its last 16 days. Shorts stocks that moved a lot either way recently, so it is hard to read cleanly.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#74
plain_english: Outputs -1 or 0. -1 (short) when the 15-day correlation of close with 37-day summed 30-day dollar volume ranks below the 11-day correlation of (almost pure) vwap rank with volume rank. Shorts stocks whose fast price-volume link beats their slow price-liquidity link.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#75
plain_english: Outputs 1 or 0. 1 (buy side) when the 4-day vwap-volume correlation ranks below the 12-day correlation of low rank with 50-day dollar volume rank. Buys stocks whose fast price-volume link is weak relative to the slow liquidity link: the mirror of #74.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#76
plain_english: The larger of two signals, flipped: the rank of the 1-day change in vwap (smoothed 11 days), and a heavily smoothed time rank of the 8-day correlation between sector-relative low and 81-day dollar volume. Shorts recent risers or stocks with an unusually strong sector-relative price-liquidity link.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Needs a sector map (indneutralize): use CoinGecko categories, or skip and demean across all coins. adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#77
formula: min(rank(decay_linear(((((high + low) / 2) + high) - (vwap + high)), 20.0451)), rank(decay_linear(correlation(((high + low) / 2), adv40, 3.1614), 5.64125)))
plain_english: The smaller of two smoothed ranks: the day's midpoint minus vwap (smoothed 20 days; the two highs in the formula cancel), and the 3-day correlation of the midpoint with 40-day dollar volume (smoothed 5 days). High only when both are high: trading below the middle of the range plus a positive price-liquidity link → buy.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#78
plain_english: The rank of the 6-day correlation of 19-day summed prices (low/vwap blend) with 19-day summed 40-day dollar volume, raised to the power of the rank of the 5-day vwap-volume rank correlation. High when the slow price-liquidity link is strong and the fast price-volume link is weak → buy.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#79
plain_english: Outputs 1 or 0. 1 (buy side) when the 1-day change in sector-relative price (close/open blend) ranks below the 14-day correlation between vwap's 3-day position and 150-day dollar volume's 9-day position. Favors stocks that did not rise versus their sector today.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Needs a sector map (indneutralize): use CoinGecko categories, or skip and demean across all coins. adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#80
plain_english: Rank of the direction (+1 or -1) of the 4-day change in industry-relative price (mostly the open), raised to the power of where the 5-day correlation of high with 10-day dollar volume sits in its last 5 days, flipped. Rising versus its industry → short.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Needs a sector map (indneutralize): use CoinGecko categories, or skip and demean across all coins. adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#81
plain_english: Outputs -1 or 0. Left side: the 8-day correlation of vwap with 49-day summed 10-day dollar volume, wrapped in ranks, a 4th power, a 14-day product and a log. -1 (short) when that ranks below the 5-day vwap-volume rank correlation.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#82
plain_english: The smaller of two signals, flipped: the rank of the smoothed 1-day change in the open (14-day smoothing), and a time rank of the smoothed 17-day correlation between sector-relative volume and the open. Shorts only when both are high: rising opens plus a strong volume-open link. The open is mixed with itself (0.63 × open + 0.37 × open).
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Needs a sector map (indneutralize): use CoinGecko categories, or skip and demean across all coins.

name: Alpha#83
plain_english: Let R = today's high-low range as a share of the 5-day average close. Score = rank of R two days ago × rank of volume × (vwap - close) / R. Positive when the close is below vwap (buy), larger on heavy volume, smaller when today's range is wide.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#84
plain_english: Where vwap's distance below its 15-day high sits in its last 20 days (between 0 and 1), raised to the power of the 4-day price change in dollars. Because the base is below 1, a 4-day rise shrinks the score toward 0 and a 4-day fall pushes it above 1, so it mostly buys recent losers. A base of exactly 0 with a falling price blows up.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha#85
plain_english: The rank of the 9-day correlation of a high/close blend with 30-day dollar volume, raised to the power of the rank of the 7-day correlation between the midpoint's 3-day position and volume's 10-day position. Like #78: strong slow price-liquidity link and weak fast price-volume link → buy.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#86
plain_english: Outputs -1 or 0. -1 (short) when how far the close is above vwap outranks where the 6-day correlation of close with 14-day summed dollar volume sits in its last 20 days. Shorts stocks closing above their average price. The two opens in the formula cancel.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#87
plain_english: The larger of two signals, flipped: the rank of the smoothed 1-day change in a close/vwap blend, and a time rank of the smoothed absolute 13-day correlation between industry-relative 81-day dollar volume and the close. Shorts today's risers or stocks with a strong liquidity-price link of either sign.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Needs a sector map (indneutralize): use CoinGecko categories, or skip and demean across all coins. adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#88
plain_english: The smaller of two signals: the smoothed rank of (open rank + low rank) minus (high rank + close rank), high after an intraday drop; and a short time rank of the smoothed correlation between the close's 8-day position and 60-day dollar volume's 20-day position. High only when both are high → buy.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#89
plain_english: Two time ranks subtracted: the smoothed 6-day correlation of the low with 10-day dollar volume, minus the smoothed 3-day change in industry-relative vwap. Buys stocks with a strong price-liquidity link that have not risen versus their industry. The low is mixed with itself (0.97 × low + 0.03 × low).
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Needs a sector map (indneutralize): use CoinGecko categories, or skip and demean across all coins. adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#90
plain_english: Rank of the close minus its 4-day high (stocks at a new high rank top), raised to the power of where the 5-day correlation of subindustry-relative 40-day dollar volume with the low sits in its last 3 days, flipped. At or near a 4-day high → short.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Needs a sector map (indneutralize): use CoinGecko categories, or skip and demean across all coins. adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#91
plain_english: Two parts subtracted and flipped: a double-smoothed 9-day correlation of industry-relative close with volume (time rank over 4 days), minus the rank of the smoothed 4-day correlation of vwap with 30-day dollar volume. Short when the industry-relative price-volume link is strong; buy when the plain price-liquidity link is strong.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Needs a sector map (indneutralize): use CoinGecko categories, or skip and demean across all coins. adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#92
plain_english: The smaller of two time ranks: how often lately the day closed with a big down candle (fell from the open by more than half the day's range; smoothed 14 days), and the smoothed 7-day correlation of low rank with 30-day dollar volume rank. High only when both are high → buy.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#93
plain_english: A ratio: a time rank of the smoothed 17-day correlation between industry-relative vwap and 81-day dollar volume, divided by the rank of the smoothed 2-day change in a close/vwap blend. Strong price-liquidity link and no recent rise → buy.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Needs a sector map (indneutralize): use CoinGecko categories, or skip and demean across all coins. adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#94
plain_english: Rank of how far vwap is above its 11-day low, raised to the power of a short time rank of the 18-day correlation between vwap's 19-day position and 60-day dollar volume's 4-day position, flipped. Far above the recent low → short.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#95
plain_english: Outputs 1 or 0. 1 (buy side) when how far the open is above its 12-day low ranks below an 11-day time rank of the (5th-powered) 12-day correlation of 19-day summed midpoints with 19-day summed 40-day dollar volume. Favors stocks still near their recent low.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#96
plain_english: The larger of two time ranks, flipped: the smoothed 3-day vwap-volume rank correlation, and the smoothed timing (days since its peak) of a 3-day correlation between the close's 7-day position and 60-day dollar volume's 4-day position. Shorts stocks with an unusually strong recent price-volume link.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#97
plain_english: Two parts subtracted and flipped: the rank of the smoothed 3-day change in industry-relative price (low/vwap blend), minus a heavily smoothed time rank of the 4-day correlation between the low's 7-day position and 60-day dollar volume's 17-day position. Rising versus its industry → short.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Needs a sector map (indneutralize): use CoinGecko categories, or skip and demean across all coins. adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#98
plain_english: Two smoothed ranks subtracted: the 4-day correlation of vwap with 26-day summed 5-day dollar volume, minus a smoothed time rank of when (within 8 days) the 20-day open-liquidity rank correlation hit its low. Mostly buys stocks whose price tracks liquidity closely.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#99
plain_english: Outputs -1 or 0. -1 (short) when the 8-day correlation of 19-day summed midpoints with 19-day summed 60-day dollar volume ranks below the 6-day correlation of the low with volume. Like #74: shorts stocks whose fast price-volume link beats the slow price-liquidity link.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#100
formula: (0 - (1 * (((1.5 * scale(indneutralize(indneutralize(rank(((((close - low) - (high - close)) / (high - low)) * volume)), IndClass.subindustry), IndClass.subindustry))) - scale(indneutralize((correlation(close, rank(adv20), 5) - rank(ts_argmin(close, 30))), IndClass.subindustry))) * (volume / adv20))))
plain_english: Two scaled, subindustry-relative parts: where the close sits in the day's range times volume, ranked (weight 1.5; neutralized twice, which is the same as once), minus \[the 5-day correlation of close with dollar-volume rank, minus the rank of how many days ago the 30-day low was\]. Flipped and multiplied by today's relative volume. Closing near the high on heavy volume, versus peers → short. An industry-relative upgrade of #60.
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas
crypto_note: Needs a sector map (indneutralize): use CoinGecko categories, or skip and demean across all coins. adv{d} = average daily dollar volume: use the average quote volume (USDT).

name: Alpha#101
plain_english: Today's candle body divided by today's range (the 0.001 avoids dividing by zero): +1 = opened at the low and closed at the high, -1 = the reverse. Buys stocks that rose during the day. The paper calls it a momentum alpha traded the next day (delay-1).
source: Kakushadze - 101 Formulaic Alphas

name: Alpha1
plain_english: 6-day correlation between ranked 1-day volume growth (log) and ranked intraday return (close vs open), flipped. Volume jumps on up-candles -> short; on down-candles -> buy. Near-copy of 101 #2 (1-day instead of 2-day volume change).
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)

name: Alpha2
plain_english: Where today's close sits in the day's range (+1 at the high, -1 at the low), minus yesterday's value, flipped. Closing much nearer the high than yesterday -> short.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)

name: Alpha3
plain_english: 6-day sum of Williams accumulation/distribution: on up days add close minus the 'true low' (lower of low and yesterday's close); on down days add close minus the 'true high' (a negative number). Steady buying pressure -> high.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)
crypto_note: Output is in price units: divide by close (or use % changes) before comparing coins with very different prices.

name: Alpha4
plain_english: Same formula as 101 Alpha #21. A mini Bollinger band. If the 2-day average close is above the 8-day average plus one 8-day standard deviation → -1 (short); below the 8-day average minus one standard deviation → +1 (buy). Inside the band: +1 if volume is at or above its 20-day average, else -1. Output is only +1 or -1.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)

name: Alpha5
plain_english: Same formula as 101 Alpha #26. Each day, the 5-day correlation between where volume sits in its own 5-day range and where the high sits in its own 5-day range; takes the largest of the last 3 days and flips. Volume and highs climbing together → short.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)

name: Alpha6
plain_english: Sign of the 4-day change of a mostly-open price (85% open + 15% high), ranked across assets and flipped. Rose over 4 days -> short.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)

name: Alpha7
plain_english: Ranks the 3-day largest and smallest gap of vwap above close and adds them, times the rank of the 3-day volume change. Kept closing below the average price while volume grew -> high. Near-copy of 101 #11.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)

name: Alpha8
plain_english: 4-day change of a blended price (20% mid-price + 80% vwap), ranked and flipped. Rose -> short.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)

name: Alpha9
plain_english: Ease of Movement (EMV), smoothed: change in the day's mid-price x day's range / volume. Price moving a lot on little volume -> large value.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)
crypto_note: Output is in price units: divide by close (or use % changes) before comparing coins with very different prices.

name: Alpha10
plain_english: For each of the last 5 days takes the close on up days or the 20-day volatility of returns on down days, squares it, and ranks the 5-day max. Price squared dominates, so this mostly ranks the recent up-day price level. Cousin of 101 #1.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)
formula_issues: Bracket typo: should be MAX(((RET<0)?STD(RET,20):CLOSE)^2, 5) - the 5 is the window of MAX.

name: Alpha11
plain_english: 6-day accumulation/distribution: each day's volume counts as buying when the close is near the high and as selling when near the low (close-location value x volume).
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)
crypto_note: Output is in raw volume units: use quote volume (USDT) or divide by average volume before comparing coins.

name: Alpha12
plain_english: Rank of how far today's open is above the 10-day average vwap, times minus the rank of how far the close strays from vwap. Opens high and closes far from vwap -> most negative (short). Close to 101 #5.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)

name: Alpha13
plain_english: Same formula as 101 Alpha #41. The geometric middle of the day's range (square root of high × low) minus vwap. Positive when most shares traded below the middle of the range → buy. One of the simplest in the set.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)
crypto_note: Output is in price units: divide by close (or use % changes) before comparing coins with very different prices.

name: Alpha14
plain_english: 5-day price change in price units (close minus close 5 days ago). Not scaled, so high-priced assets get bigger numbers.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)
crypto_note: Output is in price units: divide by close (or use % changes) before comparing coins with very different prices.

name: Alpha15
plain_english: Overnight gap: today's open / yesterday's close - 1.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)
crypto_note: Uses open vs yesterday's close. Crypto trades 24/7, so today's open is almost exactly yesterday's close and this gap is ~0 noise.

name: Alpha16
plain_english: Same formula as 101 Alpha #50. Each day, ranks the 5-day correlation between volume rank and vwap rank; takes the highest of the last 5 days and flips. A recent strong link between volume and price → short.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)

name: Alpha17
plain_english: Rank of how far vwap is below its 15-day high, raised to the power of the 5-day price change. Mixes 'distance from the recent high' with the recent move.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)
crypto_note: Output is in price units: divide by close (or use % changes) before comparing coins with very different prices.

name: Alpha18
plain_english: 5-day return as a ratio (close / close 5 days ago).
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)

name: Alpha19
plain_english: 5-day return; losses are measured against the old price, gains against today's price (so gains are slightly dampened).
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)

name: Alpha20
plain_english: 6-day return in %.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)

name: Alpha21
plain_english: Slope of the 6-day moving average over the last 6 days (linear regression on time). Positive = the average is rising; measures trend speed.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)
crypto_note: Output is in price units: divide by close (or use % changes) before comparing coins with very different prices.

name: Alpha22
plain_english: BIAS-6 (close vs its 6-day average, in %) minus its value 3 days ago, smoothed. Is price stretching further away from its average?
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)
formula_issues: SMEAN is a typo for SMA.

name: Alpha23
plain_english: Relative Volatility Index (RVI): share of the smoothed 20-day volatility that appeared on up days, x100. High = volatility comes mostly on rising days.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)
formula_issues: STD(CLOSE:20) is a typo for STD(CLOSE,20).

name: Alpha24
plain_english: Smoothed (SMA) 5-day price change, in price units.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)
crypto_note: Output is in price units: divide by close (or use % changes) before comparing coins with very different prices.

name: Alpha25
plain_english: Same formula as 101 Alpha #39. Bets against the 7-day price change, amplified when volume over the last 9 days (recent days weighted more) was light versus normal, then sized by 1 plus the rank of the 1-year return. Fades weekly moves made on thin volume, harder for long-term winners.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)

name: Alpha26
plain_english: How far close is below its 7-day average (reversal part), plus the 230-day correlation between vwap and the 5-day-lagged close. Like 101 #32 without the scaling.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)
crypto_note: Output is in price units: divide by close (or use % changes) before comparing coins with very different prices.

name: Alpha27
plain_english: 12-day weighted moving average of (3-day % return + 6-day % return).
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)

name: Alpha28
plain_english: KDJ J-style line: 3 x K - 2 x D, where K = smoothed position of the close inside its 9-day high-low range and D = K smoothed again. High = price near the top of its range and speeding up.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)
formula_issues: Second term typo: (MAX(HIGH,9)-TSMAX(LOW,9)) should be (TSMAX(HIGH,9)-TSMIN(LOW,9)).

name: Alpha29
plain_english: 6-day return x today's raw volume (volume-weighted momentum; big-volume assets dominate).
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)
crypto_note: Output is in raw volume units: use quote volume (USDT) or divide by average volume before comparing coins.

name: Alpha30
plain_english: Idiosyncratic volatility: 60-day regression of daily returns on the Fama-French factors (MKT, SMB, HML), then a 20-day weighted average of the squared leftovers (residuals).
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)
crypto_note: Replace Fama-French factors with crypto market / size / momentum factors (Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu).
formula_issues: Needs Fama-French factors (MKT, SMB, HML). DELAY(CLOSE) means DELAY(CLOSE,1).

name: Alpha31
plain_english: BIAS-12: % distance of the close from its 12-day average.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)

name: Alpha32
plain_english: Same formula as 101 Alpha #15. Each day, takes the 3-day correlation between the high's rank and volume's rank, ranks it, adds the last 3 days, and flips. Highs and heavy volume repeatedly arriving together → short.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)

name: Alpha33
plain_english: Same formula as 101 Alpha #52. Multiplies three parts: how much the 5-day low has dropped versus 5 days ago (a recent dip), the rank of the return from about 11 months ago to 1 month ago (classic long-term momentum that skips the last month), and where today's volume sits in its last 5 days. Buys dips in long-term winners on rising volume; shorts them when their lows are rising.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)

name: Alpha34
plain_english: 12-day average close / today's close. High when price has dropped below its average.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)

name: Alpha35
plain_english: Minimum of two ranks - smoothed 1-day open change, and smoothed 17-day open-volume correlation - flipped. (0.65 x open + 0.35 x open is just open.)
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)

name: Alpha36
plain_english: 6-day correlation of ranked volume and ranked vwap, summed over 2 days, ranked. High = price and volume moving together. Like 101 #27 without the yes/no cut.
source: Guotai Junan Securities (Li Chen, Liu Fubing) - 基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系 (Quant Topic No. 93)

name: MCAP (size)
formula: log(mcap) on the last day of the week
plain_english: Coin size. Small coins beat big coins.
evidence: Significant in the paper: smallest quintile beat largest by about 3.4% per week.
source: Liu, Tsyvinski & Wu - Common Risk Factors in Cryptocurrency
crypto_note: Tested on weekly returns before costs, including many tiny coins (cap > $1M). Re-test on liquid coins with costs.

name: PRC (price level)
formula: log(close) on the last day of the week
plain_english: Price level of one coin. Low-price coins beat high-price coins.
evidence: Significant in the paper: lowest quintile beat highest by about 3.9% per week.
source: Liu, Tsyvinski & Wu - Common Risk Factors in Cryptocurrency
crypto_note: Tested on weekly returns before costs, including many tiny coins (cap > $1M). Re-test on liquid coins with costs.

name: Short-horizon momentum (1-2 weeks)
plain_english: Coins that rose in the last 1-2 weeks keep rising for 1-2 more weeks.
evidence: Momentum significant for formation and holding up to 2 weeks; insignificant at 2-4 weeks.
source: Dobrynskaya - Cryptocurrency Momentum and Reversal
crypto_note: Crypto moves faster than stocks: momentum lives in weeks, not months.

name: Long-horizon reversal (1 month to 2 years)
plain_english: Coins that rose a lot over the past months tend to fall later (and the reverse). Stronger with longer lookbacks.
evidence: Significant reversal from 4 weeks up to 2 years lookback.
source: Dobrynskaya - Cryptocurrency Momentum and Reversal
crypto_note: Opposite of stock 12-month momentum.

name: Volume-conditioned reversal
plain_english: Bet against yesterday's move, mainly when it happened on low volume. Low-volume moves are noise that gets undone; liquidity providers get paid for absorbing them.
evidence: Returns reverse after low-volume intervals; low past volume strategies beat high past volume ones (12h and 24h bars).
source: Bianchi, Babiak & Dickerson - Trading Volume and Liquidity Provision in Cryptocurrency Markets
crypto_note: Formula here is a simple version of the idea; the paper uses portfolio sorts.

name: MAX momentum
plain_english: Coins with the biggest single-day jump recently keep doing better. This is the opposite of stocks, where lottery-like stocks underperform.
evidence: Higher max daily return -> higher future returns; robust to longer holding periods.
source: Li, Urquhart, Wang & Zhang - MAX Momentum in Cryptocurrency Markets
crypto_note: Sign is opposite to the stock MAX effect (CLASSIC_MAX).

name: CTREND (crypto trend factor)
formula: machine-learning combination of many price and volume technical indicators over several horizons (see paper)
plain_english: Combine lots of moving-average, momentum and volume signals into one trend score with a model. One of the few crypto signals shown to survive trading costs.
evidence: Predicts returns; not explained by known factors; survives costs; works in big, liquid coins (3,000+ coins).
source: Fieberg, Liedtke, Poddig, Walker & Zaremba - A Trend Factor for the Cross Section of Cryptocurrency Returns
venue: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 60(7)
crypto_note: Good template for what your LLM loop + factor combination can become.

name: Crypto value and network adoption
formula: on-chain activity (users, addresses, transactions) relative to market cap; growth of adoption
plain_english: Crypto version of 'cheap vs expensive': how much real network use you get per dollar of market cap.
evidence: Strong value and network-adoption premia; momentum only in the largest coins, reversal in others (4,000+ assets).
source: Cong, Karolyi, Tang & Zhao - Value Premium, Network Adoption, and Factor Pricing of Crypto Assets
crypto_note: Needs on-chain data per chain; skip for a first demo.

name: Crypto carry (futures basis / funding)
formula: annualized (futures or perp price / spot price - 1); for perps use ts_mean(funding_rate, 3 days)
plain_english: How much extra longs pay to hold leveraged positions. High carry = crowded, trend-chasing longs.
evidence: Carry averages above 10% a year and swings a lot; driven by leveraged trend-chasers and limited arbitrage capital.
data_needed: Funding rate or futures + spot prices
source: Schmeling, Schrimpf & Todorov - Crypto Carry
crypto_note: Binance funding history is free on data.binance.vision.

name: Perp premium (perp vs spot gap)
plain_english: How far the perpetual future trades above spot. The funding rate is designed to push this gap back to zero.
evidence: Theory and evidence on why perp prices deviate from spot and how funding closes the gap.
source: He, Manela, Ross & von Wachter - Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures
crypto_note: Binance premiumIndexKlines give this directly.

name: Time-series momentum (market)
plain_english: Market timing, not stock picking: when the whole crypto market (or BTC) went up last week, it tends to go up next week.
evidence: Strong time-series momentum in crypto market returns.
source: Liu & Tsyvinski - Risks and Returns of Cryptocurrency
crypto_note: Use to decide how much to hold in total, not which coin to pick.

name: Investor attention
formula: Google search volume (or social posts) for the coin, change vs its recent average
plain_english: When people suddenly search for a coin much more, future returns move with it.
evidence: Attention proxies strongly forecast future crypto returns.
source: Liu & Tsyvinski - Risks and Returns of Cryptocurrency
crypto_note: Google Trends is free but rate-limited; good later add-on.

name: Taker buy ratio
plain_english: Share of trading where buyers were the aggressive side (they crossed the spread). High = eager buyers.
source: Practitioner idea (no specific paper checked)
crypto_note: This column is already inside every Binance kline file.

name: Average trade size
plain_english: Dollars per trade. Rising trade size can mean bigger players are active.
source: Practitioner idea (no specific paper checked)

name: Funding rate level (contrarian)
plain_english: Very high funding means longs are crowded and paying a lot; bet against crowding.
source: Practitioner idea (no specific paper checked)
crypto_note: Linked to CRYPTO_SST_CARRY.

name: Funding rate change
plain_english: Is leverage demand rising or falling?
source: Practitioner idea (no specific paper checked)

name: Open interest change
plain_english: How fast new leveraged positions are being opened.
source: Practitioner idea (no specific paper checked)
crypto_note: The live API only keeps 30 days; use the data.binance.vision archive for history.

name: Open interest vs price divergence
plain_english: Price up while open interest falls = short covering (weak rally); price up with open interest rising = new longs.
source: Practitioner idea (no specific paper checked)

name: Top-trader long/short ratio (contrarian)
plain_english: When most big accounts lean long, bet against the crowd.
source: Practitioner idea (no specific paper checked)

name: BTC-residual reversal
plain_english: Bet against only the coin's own move, after removing the part explained by BTC.
source: Practitioner idea (no specific paper checked)
crypto_note: Cleaner than plain reversal because most alt moves are just BTC moves.

name: Beta to BTC (low-beta)
plain_english: Crypto version of betting-against-beta: prefer coins that move less with BTC.
source: Practitioner idea (no specific paper checked)

name: Market beta (CAPM)
plain_english: How much an asset moves with the market.
source: Sharpe - Capital Asset Prices
crypto_note: Use BTC or a crypto market index as the market.

name: Size (SMB)
plain_english: Small companies beat big ones.
source: Fama & French - Common Risk Factors in the Returns on Stocks and Bonds
crypto_note: Works in crypto too (CRYPTO_LTW_MCAP). Market cap from CoinGecko.

name: Value (HML)
plain_english: Cheap companies (high book-to-market) beat expensive ones.
source: Fama & French - Common Risk Factors in the Returns on Stocks and Bonds
crypto_note: Coins have no book value; see CRYPTO_CKTZ_VALUE for an on-chain version.

name: Profitability (RMW)
plain_english: Profitable firms beat unprofitable ones.
source: Fama & French - A Five-Factor Asset Pricing Model
crypto_note: No crypto equivalent (protocol revenue is a distant cousin).

name: Investment (CMA)
plain_english: Firms that grow assets slowly beat fast-growing ones.
source: Fama & French - A Five-Factor Asset Pricing Model
crypto_note: Token supply growth (inflation) is a loose analog.

name: Momentum 12-1 month
plain_english: Last year's winners (skipping the latest month) keep winning.
source: Jegadeesh & Titman - Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers; Carhart (1997)
crypto_note: In crypto, momentum works over 1-4 weeks; 1-month+ lookbacks tend to reverse (CRYPTO_DOB_REV).

name: Short-term reversal (1 month)
plain_english: Last month's losers bounce back.
source: Jegadeesh - Evidence of Predictable Behavior of Security Returns
crypto_note: Use 1-7 day windows in crypto; 1-4 week windows show momentum instead.

name: Betting against beta
plain_english: Low-beta assets earn more per unit of risk than high-beta ones.
source: Frazzini & Pedersen - Betting Against Beta
crypto_note: Use beta to BTC (CRYPTO_PR_BTC_BETA).

name: Amihud illiquidity
plain_english: Hard-to-trade assets pay a premium.
source: Amihud - Illiquidity and Stock Returns
crypto_note: Same as CRYPTO_LTW_DAMIHUD (not significant there). Use quote volume.

name: Idiosyncratic volatility
formula: ts_std(residual of ret on Fama-French 3 factors, 21)
plain_english: Stocks with high stock-specific volatility earn LOW future returns.
source: Ang, Hodrick, Xing & Zhang - The Cross-Section of Volatility and Expected Returns
crypto_note: Use a crypto market factor; not significant in CRYPTO_LTW_IDIOVOL.

name: MAX (lottery) effect
plain_english: Stocks with a huge recent one-day jump (lottery-like) underperform.
source: Bali, Cakici & Whitelaw - Maxing Out
crypto_note: Sign flips in crypto: see CRYPTO_LUWZ_MAX.

name: 52-week high
plain_english: Assets trading near their 52-week high keep doing well.
source: George & Hwang - The 52-Week High and Momentum Investing
crypto_note: Use 365 days in crypto (it trades every day).

name: Turnover
plain_english: Heavily traded stocks earn lower future returns.
source: Datar, Naik & Radcliffe - Liquidity and Stock Returns: An Alternative Test
crypto_note: Use quote volume / market cap (CRYPTO_LTW_VOLSCALED).
